2027-03-02.title: Tuesday of the fourth week of the Great Fast
readings: The birth of Isaac: God has brought laughter
Clothed with Christ, heirs according to the promise
Woe to the cities that did not repent
2027-03-02.verse: God has brought laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me.
theo: After twenty-five years of waiting, the promise is kept. “The Lord dealt with Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did for Sarah as he had promised. Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the time of which God had spoken to him.” Notice how often the reading repeats it: as he had said, as he had promised, as God had spoken. Abraham names the boy Isaac, which means “he laughs.” Years before, Sarah had laughed in disbelief behind the tent door; now she laughs for joy: “God has brought laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me.” The same woman, the same laughter, but turned inside out by the faithfulness of God. Early Fathers such as St Ambrose saw in Isaac, the son of promise born when nature had given up hope, a figure of Christ, the true joy of the world (in substance). The Great Fast is not a season of gloom; it prepares us for the laughter of Easter, when God keeps his greatest promise.

Paul tells us whose children we are: “for in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith. As many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.” In our baptism we were clothed in a white garment; in Christ there is “no longer Jew or Greek, there is no longer slave or free, there is no longer male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus. And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s offspring, heirs according to the promise.” The laughter of Sarah has become the inheritance of every baptized person. But an inheritance can be neglected. In the Gospel Jesus reproaches the towns around the lake, Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum, which had seen most of his miracles and still did not change: “if the deeds of power done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.” We who have received the sacraments, the Word and the Holy Qurbono every week have seen more than Tyre and Sidon ever saw. The Fast asks whether all that grace has changed us.
outline: Ask: what promise of God are you still waiting for?
Isaac is born; Sarah's laughter of joy.
Children of God, heirs of the promise.
live: Find out the date of your baptism and thank God for it today; if you have your baptismal candle or photo, bring it to the family prayer corner.
Name one grace you have received again and again, and one change it should produce in you; make that change this week.
2027-03-02.prayer: Faithful God, you did for Sarah as you had promised, and you turned her laughter of doubt into laughter of joy. You have clothed us with Christ in baptism and made us heirs of your promise. Do not let the many graces we receive pass over us without fruit. Give us repentant hearts in this Great Fast, and bring us at last to the joy of the Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Each Holy Qurbono is a deed of power done in our midst: Christ himself, truly present, given to children of God who were clothed with him in baptism.

quick: God kept his promise: Sarah bore Isaac, and her laughter became joy.
In baptism we were clothed with Christ and became heirs of the promise to Abraham.
Jesus reproaches the towns that saw his miracles and did not repent.
2027-03-02.action: Find the date of your baptism and give thanks for it.
2027-03-02.question: Which of God's graces to me has not yet changed my life?

family.explain: Abraham and Sarah waited many, many years for a baby. They were very old. But God had promised, and God kept his promise: baby Isaac was born! His name means “he laughs,” because Sarah laughed with happiness. God always keeps his promises.
family.intention: We pray for couples who are waiting for a child, and for all who are waiting for God's help.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know the day each of us was baptized? Let us find out together.”

illus: A couple in Pathanamthitta waited eleven years for a child. Every First Friday they went to the same small chapel, and the old sacristan, who knew their story, would nod to them as they came in. When their daughter was finally born, they brought her to the chapel at two weeks old. The sacristan, now walking with a stick, looked at the baby and began to laugh, and then to cry, and then to laugh again. He said: I have been praying for this child for eleven years too. You did not know that, did you?

pm.open: Faithful Father, you keep every promise. Fill us with the joy of your children. Amen.
share: The Lord did for Sarah as he had promised (Genesis 21:1). Which promise of God am I still waiting to see fulfilled?
As many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:27). Do I live as someone clothed with Christ?
They would have repented long ago (Matthew 11:21). What grace have I received many times without changing?
pm.resp: Lord, keep your promise in us.
interc: For all who have lost hope after long waiting.
For the newly baptized and for parents and godparents.
For the conversion of hearts in our parish this Lent.
For unity among all the baptized, one in Christ Jesus.
pm.close: Father, you made us your children in Christ and heirs of the promise to Abraham. Let the graces we receive bear fruit in repentance, and turn our tears into the laughter of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the Lord did for Sarah as he had promised. Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age (Genesis 21:1–2). After long years of waiting, God kept his word.
Sarah once laughed in disbelief; now she says: God has brought laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me (Genesis 21:6). The Fast prepares us for the laughter of Easter.

Paul says we are all children of God through faith: as many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ; you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise (Galatians 3:26–29).
But Jesus warns the towns that saw his miracles and did not repent: woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! (Matthew 11:21). We have received so much grace. In this Fast, let it change us. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham and Sarah waited a very long time for a baby, and God gave them Isaac. His name means “he laughs,” because they were so happy! When you were baptized, God made you his child too. That is a reason to be happy every day.

intro: Theme: “God has brought laughter for me.”
The birth of Isaac, the children of God clothed with Christ, and the warning to the towns that saw much and did not change.

q: God is not a human being, that he should lie, or a mortal, that he should change his mind. Has he promised, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
For nothing will be impossible with God.
points.apply: Write down one promise of God from Scripture and pray it every day this week.

q: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness,
See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises quietly before the Holy Qurbono this Sunday.

q: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity that he had said he would bring upon them; and he did not do it.
From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required; and from the one to whom much has been entrusted, even more will be demanded.
points.apply: Prepare this week for a good confession, naming the graces you have wasted.

concl: God keeps his promises and turns our sorrow into laughter.
Those clothed with Christ are called to let his grace change them.
2027-03-02.resolve: Live the rest of the Fast as a child of God who does not waste grace.
